method: Two independent material paintings, interpreted in Aseprite; approved objects unchanged

prompts.meadow: Create a production SOURCE MATERIAL PAINTING for Valdoria, a sophisticated medieval 2D three-quarter pixel art RPG, matching the rich handcrafted pixel clusters of detailed Quaternius-scale medieval stone-and-timber houses and realistically voluminous painted pixel oak trees. This is NOT a scene, illustration, screenshot, diorama, or big map. Only a square uninterrupted patch of low MEADOW GROUND viewed from near overhead with the subtle vertical foreshortening appropriate for 3/4 RPG ground. Entire canvas opaque grass surface, no border, no text, no props, no trees, no flowers, no rocks, no path. Pixel-art craft, no blurry airbrush, no photorealism, no vector/cartoon. Build organic interlocking flat swards with groups of very short blades and creeping tiny leaves; substantial quiet areas of worn shorter grass, small soft exposed olive-earth irregular pockets woven between grass; deliberate medium-scale overlapping grassy masses with a few dark lower/right contact pixels and warmer upper-left ridges, NOT raised mounds or bushes. Rich but CONTROLLED mid olive greens, restrained gold-green tips, cooler dark recesses, no neon or black outlines. Finely constructed 1-3 pixel microclusters subordinated to large calm mid-value fields; no random noise sprinkled evenly; no grids, no evenly spaced clumps, no iconic repeated tufts, no continuous outlines, no obvious directional stripe. Surface reads as richly authored carpet of low growing groundcover, supportive and quieter than architecture. Fairly even illumination upper left, no spotlight, no vignette or central focal feature. Target intended native interpretation 384x384 pixels from this master; preserve crisp clusters. Make all four edges visually compatible with neighboring arbitrary meadow surfaces, no obvious frame or dark fringe. Do not create a landscape horizon or camera perspective vanishing point.
prompts.earth: A square SOURCE MATERIAL PAINTING, uninterrupted worn earth ground, for a sophisticated medieval three-quarter 2D pixel art RPG called Valdoria. NOT a scene, not a screenshot, not a road network illustration, no grass border, no trees or props, no text, no frame. Entire opaque canvas shows naturally compacted warm grey-ochre dirt surface with worn flattened smooth areas separated by shallow granular seams, small broken angular soil flakes, partially embedded tiny pale grey stones and a few tiny loose chips. A surface of earth, NOT a uniform gravel field and NOT large cobblestones. Coherent groups of grains with deliberate quiet compacted patches; slightly darker earth in shallow hollows and brighter upper-left lips on occasional small soil breaks; irregular horizontal compression appropriate to near-overhead 3/4 ground, no deep relief. Surface macro and medium forms should be gently oriented, oblique worn microtraces and clustered aggregate, but NO literal wheel ruts painted across the canvas: the game tool adds path-following wear separately. Warm clay/brown ochre midtones, modest saturation; darkest cracks cool brown, lightest sparse plane edges soft sandstone, no dark black outlines or orange candy look. Rich authored crisp pixel-art clusters consistent with finely painted medieval stone-and-timber buildings, substantial fractured pixel boulders and detailed oak trees. Hierarchical detail, no uniform white-noise speckles, no photo scan, no blurry render, no vector cartoon. Broad even illumination upper left, no vignette or focal spotlight. Make full surface all the way to edges, no outline. Intended native interpretation at384x384 pixels, supporting player gameplay legibility. Material should feel worked, walked on and embedded, not clean flat brown paint.
